reports.summary:
• Verdict: the internet was reliable this week, with 99.9% WAN uptime over 2,065 checks. There was one measured outage of 0.5 min and no automatic restarts or router reboots. The one thing to watch is the router's own DNS: it timed out 5 times between Nov 13 21:50 and Nov 14 23:35, and recovered each time.
• Versus last week, the connection was slightly less clean. Last week had 100% uptime and no disconnects; this week the router logged 2 WAN disconnects. Ping spiked to a maximum of 1,149.77 ms (previously 37.3 ms), and minimum line quality dropped to 0% (previously 100%). Average jitter rose from 0.31 to 0.54 ms, and peak router memory use rose from 63.8% to 74.7%. Speedtests stayed steady at about 934/303 Mbps with 2.2 ms latency.
• Traffic was 222.4 GB down and 18.7 GB up, compared with 280.6 GB and 15.9 GB the week before. The busiest day was Nov 15 with 57.5 GB down.
• The biggest user by far was TV 2 with 112.0 GB, about half of all downloads. Next were Phone 6 (25.5 GB), Phone 4 (15.4 GB), Phone 5 (12.9 GB) and Laptop 2 (8.0 GB). The TV also had 54.8% of its DNS queries blocked and was flagged on Nov 15 for contacting new domains. That is likely ad/telemetry related, but worth a glance.
• DNS filtering covered 4 of 7 days and blocked 10.2% of 265,353 queries, which is a routine rate. Laptop 4 made the most queries (39,516, 17.2% blocked). DNS data was not collected for the previous week, so there is no comparison.
• Three new devices appeared:
• Smart device 1 (Espressif, Nov 9)
• Camera 3 (camera, Nov 11)
• an Apple iPhone (Nov 12), which also triggered an iot_lan event on Nov 15
• Recommendation 1: look into the router DNS timeouts together with the higher memory use and the ping spike. Check the router's logs and memory, and consider a planned reboot if the timeouts continue.
• Recommendation 2: confirm what Smart device 1 is. If it and the Reolink camera are IoT devices, move them to the IoT network/VLAN.
